t: You're on Snow Hill, a street in the City of London. In the past it was the site of one of the City's water conduits, which on days of great celebration was made to run with red and white wine. The last time was the anniversary of George the Second's coronation in 1727. Two notable people were born here. Richard Bowdler Sharpe became a curator of birds at the British Museum of natural history, and several bird species are named after him. Austin Osman Spare was an artist and occultist, known for his clear line and for developing techniques such as automatic drawing.
